page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Identify a, b, c and find √(a² + b²)
steps.margin_note: First mark. (3√3)² is 27, not 9. With 169 it makes 196, and √196 is exactly 14 — a whole number, which is the sign that the squaring was done correctly.
steps.memory_tip: (3√3)² = 9 × 3 = 27, and 169 + 27 = 196 = 14². Here the root comes out whole, which makes the arithmetic easy to check.
lines: Given f(x) = 13 cos x + 3√3 sin x − 4
Compare with a cos x + b sin x + c:

accept: three root three squared is twenty seven so one sixty nine plus twenty seven is one ninety six
the root of one ninety six is fourteen
a is thirteen, b is three root three and c is minus four
three root three square ante twenty seven, root one ninety six is fourteen

steps.why: The values of a cos x + b sin x fill the whole interval from −√(a² + b²) to √(a² + b²), so this one square root carries the answer.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as √196 instead of 14.

steps.label: Write the range as an interval
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The −4 moves both ends of the interval: the low end to −18 and the high end to 10. Write it as an interval, smaller number first.
steps.memory_tip: Both ends move by the constant: −4 − 14 = −18 and −4 + 14 = 10, so the range is [−18, 10].

recall.must_convey: That the range is [−18, 10], because the constant −4 moves both −14 and 14 down by 4.
accept: minus four minus fourteen is minus eighteen and minus four plus fourteen is ten
the range is minus eighteen to ten
both ends of the interval move down by four
rendu ends four thakkuva avuthai, minus eighteen to ten
the answer is the closed interval from minus eighteen to ten

steps.why: 13 cos x + 3√3 sin x takes every value between −14 and 14 as x varies, and subtracting 4 moves that whole interval down by 4.
common_mistakes: Writing the range as [−14, 14] and ignoring the −4.
